title: Cendol (shaved ice with pandan jellies, coconut milk and palm sugar)

ingredients.name: coconut milk, with a pinch of salt
cooked red beans or sweetcorn, optional

steps: Blend the pandan leaves with the water, strain, and press out all the green juice. You need about 300 ml.
Whisk the rice flour, starch and salt into the pandan juice, then cook over low heat, stirring constantly, until it thickens to a thick, glossy paste.
Press the hot mixture through a colander with large holes straight into a bowl of iced water, so it falls in short green droplets. Leave to set for 5 minutes, then drain.
Melt the palm sugar with the water over low heat and strain it into a clean pan, simmering for a few minutes until syrupy. Cool.
Pile shaved ice into four bowls, add the cendol jellies and any beans or corn, then pour over the coconut milk and drizzle generously with palm sugar syrup.
Serve immediately, before the ice melts.

title: Chicken satay (grilled skewers with peanut sauce)

ingredients.name: boneless chicken thighs, cut into small strips
bamboo skewers, soaked in water for 30 minutes
dried chillies, soaked in hot water until soft

steps: Blend the lemongrass, 2 shallots, 2 cloves of garlic and the galangal into a paste, then mix with the turmeric, coriander, cumin, 1 tbsp sugar, salt and 1 tbsp oil. Coat the chicken and marinate for at least 2 hours.
Thread the chicken tightly onto the soaked skewers.
For the sauce, grind the peanuts coarsely, and blend the soaked chillies with the remaining shallots and garlic into a paste.

Fry the chilli paste in the remaining oil for 4 minutes until fragrant and the oil separates. Add the water, peanuts, tamarind and remaining sugar, and simmer for 10 minutes until thick, adding salt to taste.
Grill the skewers over medium-high charcoal or in a hot grill pan for 3 to 4 minutes per side, brushing with a little oil, until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot with the peanut sauce, cucumber and onion wedges.

title: Nasi dagang (coconut rice with tuna curry, Terengganu style)

ingredients.name: tamarind pulp soaked in 100 ml hot water, strained
cucumber and pickled vegetables (acar), to serve

steps: Wash both kinds of rice and soak them for 2 hours with the fenugreek seeds, then drain.
Steam the rice with 200 ml of the coconut milk, the shallots, ginger and half the salt until tender, about 30 minutes, fluffing once halfway.
Blend the chillies, garlic, 1 stalk lemongrass and turmeric into a paste and fry in the oil for 5 minutes until fragrant.
Add the remaining coconut milk, the other lemongrass stalk bruised, 150 ml water, the tamarind liquid, sugar and remaining salt, and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the tuna and cook for 8 to 10 minutes until just done, without letting the coconut milk boil hard.
Serve the coconut rice with the tuna curry and cool cucumber and acar on the side.

title: Nasi kerabu (blue herb rice from Kelantan)

ingredients.name: fresh grated coconut, dry-toasted until golden and ground (kerisik)
mixed fresh herbs, finely sliced (mint, coriander, basil; Vietnamese coriander if you can find it)
fried or grilled fish, salted egg and sambal, to serve

steps: Steep the dried butterfly pea flowers in 600 ml of hot water for 10 minutes until deep blue, then strain, pressing the flowers.
Rinse the rice and cook it in the blue water with the lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves and salt until tender and fluffy, then fluff with a fork.
Toast the grated coconut in a dry pan, stirring constantly, until golden, then pound or grind it to a coarse powder.
Prepare the raw vegetables and herbs, slicing them as finely as you can.
Mound the blue rice on each plate and surround it with piles of the herbs, long beans, sprouts, cucumber and onion.
Add a piece of grilled fish, half a salted egg and a spoonful of sambal, sprinkle with the toasted coconut, and toss everything together at the table.

title: Otak-otak (spiced fish cakes grilled in banana leaf)

ingredients.name: firm white fish fillet or mackerel, minced
banana leaves, softened over a flame, and toothpicks

steps: Blend the chillies, shallots, garlic, lemongrass, galangal and turmeric into a smooth paste.
Mix the fish with the paste, coconut milk, egg, rice flour, lime leaves, sugar and salt, and beat vigorously until the mixture is sticky and cohesive.
Cut the banana leaves into 20 cm rectangles and soften them briefly over a gas flame or in hot water so they do not tear.
Spoon 3 tbsp of the mixture onto each leaf and fold into a neat flat packet, securing the ends with toothpicks.
Grill the packets over medium coals or in a hot pan for 4 to 5 minutes per side until the leaf is charred and the filling is firm.
Serve hot, opening the leaf to eat the soft, fragrant fish cake straight from it.

title: Pan mee (hand-torn noodles in anchovy broth)

ingredients.name: dried anchovies (ikan bilis), heads and guts removed
leafy greens such as sweet potato leaves or spinach
chilli flakes fried in oil, to serve

steps: Mix the flour, egg, water and salt into a smooth dough, knead for 5 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Toast half of the anchovies in a dry pan, then simmer them with the other half in the water for 25 minutes. Strain and season with soy sauce.
Fry the remaining anchovies in a little oil until crisp and set aside, then use the same oil to fry the garlic until golden.
Stir-fry the pork with the mushrooms for 5 minutes, adding a splash of soy sauce.
Flatten pieces of the dough with your fingers and tear them into thin, irregular strips straight into the simmering broth. Cook for 3 minutes, adding the greens in the last minute.
Poach the eggs in the broth, then serve the noodles topped with pork, mushrooms, crispy anchovies, garlic oil and chilli flakes.

title: Roti canai (Malaysian flaky flatbread)

ingredients.name: warm milk or water, plus a little more if needed
oil for coating the dough balls
dhal or chicken curry, to serve

steps: Stir the flour, salt and sugar together, then work in the egg, the milk and 1 tbsp of the ghee until a soft, slightly tacky dough forms. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth and stretchy.
Divide the dough into 6 balls, roll each in oil until well coated, and leave them in a covered, oiled container to rest for at least 2 hours so the gluten relaxes.
On an oiled work surface, flatten one ball with oiled fingers, then stretch it outward, slapping and pulling until it is paper-thin and almost see-through.
Brush the sheet with ghee, then fold in the sides and ends to make a small square, or twist the sheet into a rope and coil it into a spiral. Rest the shaped pieces for 10 minutes.
Flatten each piece a little, then cook on a medium-hot greased griddle for 2 minutes per side until golden and crisp at the edges.
Hold the hot roti between your hands and push the edges together a few times to crumple and open up the layers. Serve at once with dhal or curry.

title: Teh tarik (Malaysian pulled milk tea)

ingredients.name: strong loose black tea (or 4 tea bags)
sweetened condensed milk, or to taste

steps: Pour the boiling water over the tea and steep for 5 minutes, then strain into a jug.
Divide the condensed milk and evaporated milk between two heatproof cups or jugs.
Pour the hot tea over the milk and stir to dissolve.
Holding one jug high and the other low, pour the tea back and forth between them in a long stream about six times. The pouring cools the tea slightly and creates a thick froth.
Serve in glasses while hot and frothy.
